A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GENEB study of 40 genomic models on 100 tasks. Their main text, Appendices A–F, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison; the additional page in v4 does not indicate missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original full-data and few-shot benchmarking results, together with probe comparisons, regularization sensitivity tests, and model-factor analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmarking and supplementary experimental results and reports revised analyses of model size, tokenization, and pretraining.

M1.justification: GENEB retains frozen embeddings, mean pooling, and logistic-regression probing. Revised descriptions of evaluated models do not establish changes to the benchmark procedure, model implementations, or checkpoints.

E1.justification: Appendix B retains the same 100 classification tasks from nine benchmark sources across 13 categories. The changed pretraining-corpus label for GPT2-Gene-Multi-v2 concerns a retained model and does not document new training data or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The overall 40-model roster is unchanged, but comparator pairings in Tables 15–17 are revised. For example, OMNI-DNA-300M versus eccDNAMamba is added, and GPT2-Gene-based architecture, corpus, and tokenization comparisons are removed, replaced, or reassigned.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes change, including eccDNAMamba from 1B to 537M and Caduceus-PS-131k from 2M to 8M, affecting size controls and analysis groups. Matched-pair selections also change. The probing regimes, task subsampling, and metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 revises which contrasts test architecture, pretraining, and tokenization effects, enumerating 11/9/11 pairs instead of 9/9/12. Corresponding category analyses are revised. The linear-versus-MLP, regularization-sensitivity, and micro-versus-macro robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over the same five fixed seeds and retain the same statistical reporting practices. Updated correlations and p-values are changed results, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: Section 4 changes the size-performance correlation from 0.565 to 0.573 and the count of in-domain size reversals from 31 to 25. Table 2 changes the mean multi-species advantage from +0.012 to +0.018 under revised pair selections. Appendix F also corrects individual scores and ranks, including MUTBERT’s histone rank from 11th to 8th. The underlying benchmark score matrix is largely retained.

T1.justification: The aggregation definitions, controlled-pair difference calculations, and formal specialization-score definition in Appendix F.11 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and central claims about category-dependent rankings, limited explanatory power of scale, pretraining alignment, and few-shot degradation. Revised numerical support does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F.12.13 reinterprets eccDNAMamba’s chromatin-accessibility advantage as a reversal at near-matched scale, replacing the earlier size-favored explanation. F.12.9 now explicitly acknowledges tokenization confounding in the DNA-GPT/GPT2-Gene corpus comparison. The encoder-decoder discussion also distinguishes consistent aggregate encoder advantages from category-dependent outcomes.

D1.justification: Table 4 revises parameter counts, identifies both GPT2-Gene tokenizers as BPE instead of k-mer, relabels GPT2-Gene-Multi-v2 pretraining as human, and expands DeepGene’s architecture description. These are documentation revisions; hardware disclosures, probe implementation details, and public-release plans remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Figure 1 revises the depicted comparison relationships among prior models, including a GenomeOcean-to-GENERator link. The cited-work roster and GENEB’s substantive positioning relative to existing benchmarks otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F receive targeted paragraph revisions, corrected descriptions, and standardized Mamba terminology. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 3 changes its palette and column ordering to match macro-MCC rankings. Tables 4 and 14–17 revise row ordering or membership, with limited page reflow. Most figures are retained, including size-performance plots whose old parameter placements were not updated.

improvement.justification: v4 improves interpretability by aligning several matched comparisons with revised model descriptions, clarifying confounds, and correcting Figure 3’s macro-MCC ordering and erroneous ranks in the prose. The benefit is limited by incomplete propagation of corrections: Figure 2 still places Caduceus-PS-131k near 2M parameters although Table 4 now reports 8M. The analytical clarifications provide a modest net improvement despite these remaining inconsistencies.
